### The reader 0x8004892C (sces twin 0x80048A28, +0xFC): full body

    int reader(int dev) {                 // 0x8004892C, frame 0x38
      if ((u32)dev >= 10) return -1;
      if (checker(device_table[dev]) != 0) return -1;   // busy/already-resident gate
      if (dev == 0) { size = 0x10 << shift; base = 0xFFF0 << shift; }   // OVERRIDE
      else { size = (0x10000 - device_table[dev]) << shift;
             base = device_table[dev] << shift; }
      if (*0x80065DCC == 1) { *0x80065DCC = 0; restore_dcc = 1; }   // park alt-read mode
      if (*0x80065DE8 != 0) { saved_hook = *0x80065DE8; *0x80065DE8 = 0; }  // park hook
      do {
        n = (remaining <= 0x400) ? remaining : 0x400;   // last chunk flags exit
        issuer(2, base_cursor);            // SPU transfer addr = cursor/8 (+ shadow static)
        issuer(1);                         // SPUCNT transfer mode = DMA write, guard2 = 0
        issuer(3, 0x800659A8, n);          // staging buffer; the SPU DMA write kickoff
        WaitEvent(*0x80065998);            // B0#0x0A thunk at 0x80048ACC - per chunk
        remaining -= 0x400; base_cursor += 0x400;
      } while (!last);
      if (restore_dcc) *0x80065DCC = old;  // un-park
      if (saved_hook)    *0x80065DE8 = saved_hook;
      return 0;
    }

* The 10 "devices" are SE sound banks, TOP-ALLOCATED in SPU-RAM: with shift =
  *0x80065DD8 = 3, size = (0x10000 - table[dev]) << 3 bytes and base =
  table[dev] << 3, so size + base = 0x10000 << 3 = 0x80000 EXACTLY - every
  bank ends at the 512 KiB SPU-RAM top. The table values are stored as
  0x10000 - size_units, i.e. NEGATIVE distances from the top in 8-byte units
  (the SPU transfer-address register 0x1F801DA6 encodes addr/8 - cmd 2's
  >>shift and the tables' <<3 are the same /8 law seen from both sides).
* dev 0 OVERRIDES its own table entry (0xFFFE = would be 16 B at 0x7FFF0)
  with the constants 0x10/0xFFF0 -> a 0x80-byte chunk at 0x7FF80 - the
  0x80-byte chunk step of the SE-bank chunked loader (func #56 path), now
  proven at the load site. The checker still tests the UN-overridden
  0x7FFF0<<... = table[0]<<3 address for dev 0 (retail inconsistency,
  harmless: the overlap test is conservative).
* Bank sizes (bytes, computed by the reader): dev0 0x80@0x7FF80, dev1
  0x26C0@0x7D940, dev2 0x1F40@0x7E100, dev3 0x4840@0x7B7C0, dev4
  0x6FE0@0x79020, dev5 0xADE0@0x75220, dev6 0xF6C0@0x70940, dev7
  0x18040@0x67FC0, dev8 0x18040@0x67FC0, dev9 0x3C00@0x7C400.
* TABLE CORRECTIONS (both regions byte-exact twins at delta -0x37C; sces
  complement table re-located at 0x80065AB8 by exact byte search - the
  0x80065B58 spot checks different data): the tables are U32-STRIDED (value
  + 0x0000 pad); the earlier u16 view silently read only the low halves.
  The complement law "complement = 0x10000 - table[i]" holds for 9/10 and
  FAILS at dev 2 in BOTH regions: stored 0x3D8 (984 units = 7872 B) vs
  computed 0x3E8 (1000 units = 8000 B) - a genuine retail data quirk, not a
  transcription slip. The READER never reads the complement table (it

* The checker 0x800488B4 (sces 0x800489B0): a0 = table[dev] << shift (the

### The issuer 0x8003DF54 cmd-3 kickoff: the D4_MADDR wiring CORRECTED

The issuer's prologue is the key: `sw $a2,8($sp); addiu $a2,$sp,4; ...;
sw $a0,($sp); sw $a1,4($sp)` - the THIRD arg slot is OVERWRITTEN with
$sp+4, i.e. a2 becomes a pointer to the frame pair {saved_a1, saved_a2} =
{dest, len}. The cmd-3 tail then walks THAT pair (a2 += 4; a0 = *(a2-4);
a0 = *a2):

    *0x80065E04 = dest;                        // read-state dest slot
    **0x80065DB8 = dest;                       // D4_MADDR (0x1F8010C0) = THE RAM ADDRESS
    *0x80065E08 = ceil(len/0x40);              // block count (word-exact law)
    **0x80065DBC = (ceil(len/0x40) << 16) | 0x10;   // D4_BCR (0x1F8010C4)
    **0x80065DC0 = (guard2 == 1) ? 0x01000200 : 0x01000201;  // D4_CHCR (0x1F8010C8)

The 4th-window banked reading "**0x80065DB8 = a2 (the raw length)" was a
misread of this indirection (it took the pair pointer for the value):
MADDR gets the DEST (main-RAM staging address), the LEN feeds only BCR -
hardware-correct. Two more corrections in the same tail: the DICR write
through *0x80065DC8 (0x1F801014) is `(*DICR & 0xF0FFFFFF) | 0x22000000`
(bits 29+25, consistent with psx-spx's nonzero-24..30-field stability
note) in BOTH guard2 paths - the two paths are a DUPLICATED (not folded)
block with identical semantics, and the OR constant is 0x22000000, not
the banked 0x20000000; and cmd 2 also updates the u16 SHADOW static
*0x80065DB0 (= addr >> shift, same value it stores to obj->0x1A6), which
is what cmd 0/1's spin compares obj->0x1A6 against (cap 0xF01, -2 on
timeout) - the parked-position handshake is register-vs-shadow.

Harness (repo-external, recreatable): scripts/probe_buildadsr.py (pipeline +
normalizer) and scripts/brute_buildadsr.py (grid driver) - cpp -> cc1<flags>
-> maspsx --expand-div, then a dialect-normalizing compare against the
committed retail row asm/nonmatchings/func_8004DACC.s. Normalizer laws
(same encoding, different printers): maspsx renders the 0x8000-immediate
as "-32768 & 0xFFFF"; beq $x,$zero == beqz; subu $x,$zero,$x == negu;
j $reg == jr; numeric registers == named; offsets decimal.

FOUR NEW LAWS (all measured against the retail row):

1. SIGNED-CONST LAW: retail materializes the mask constant as
   `addiu $a0,$zero,-0x8000` + `and $t1,$v0,$a0` - the original C expressed
   the 0x8000 flag masks as SIGNED values (`fC ? -0x8000 : 0` class; GCC
   never picks andi 0x8000 for these sites). Every `& 0x8000` / andi-form
   candidate is dead on arrival. The signed-sloppiness also explains the
   absent truncations: the mask webs carry 0xFFFF8000-class upper garbage
   that the final `sh` stores never see.
2. INIT-DECL LOAD-ORDER LAW: the head loads +0xC then +0x10 back-to-back
   and the +0xA load sits between mask1 and the copy. That exact order
   falls out of C89 init-decls (`int fC = s[6]; int f10 = s[8]; int t1 =
   fC ? -0x8000 : 0; int fA = s[5];`); the same reads written as
   ASSIGNMENT statements let GCC hoist the +0xA load above the mask chain
   (wrong order, reproducibly).
3. THE COPY SURVIVES: with laws 1+2 plus the statement order [copy t0 = t1;
   mask2 (its `and` fills the beqz delay slot); `if (f10) t0 = t1 | 0x4000`
   with ori reading t1 in the fallthrough], the T4 shape reproduces the
   retail body 33/35 insns at PLAIN -O2 - the copy-before-branch, the
   delay-slot and, the whole word1/word2 or-chain layout, all exact. The
   old "every shape folds the copy" was a shape statement, not an
   impossibility. -O1's documented schedule-nop + arg-move divergence
   reproduced by the harness (the TASKS note above stands).
4. THE REMAINING BLOCKER IS ONE ALLOCNO DECISION: a cyclic permutation of
   the three temps - built (mask1,copy,mask2) = ($8,$10,$9) vs retail
   ($9,$8,$10); retail's `ori` reads $9 and the copy writes $8, ours mirror.
   GCC 2.6.3's local_alloc merges the first mask's web into the copy
   target's register in every steer tried: decl-order variants (5), the
   dead-init pseudo-creation trick (the dead store is deleted and takes
   the pseudo with it), the goto-else class from the GSD round-5 lesson
   (keeps the insn order, not the allocation), a 192-combo brute force
   (load-form x copy-pos x if-body x types x dead-init x w1-order x
   f10-position), and flag axes (-O1, -fschedule-insns, -fschedule-insns2,
   -fno-delayed-branch, -fno-expensive-optimizations, -fno-cse-follow-jumps,
   -fno-thread-jumps, -fno-caller-saves, -fno-force-mem,
   -fno-rerun-cse-after-loop). Note the retail insn COUNT equals the T4
   count (35): the real source created the copy-target pseudo before
   mask1's WITHOUT any extra surviving insn - no source-level construction
   found that does that in our cc1.

## 2026-10-17 (window cron-20261017-1342): GsMapModelingData's body closes -
## indexed r[i] + field order [+0x00, +0x08, +0x10] is register-for-register
## EXACT; the corner narrows to one head instruction (i=0 / walk2 / nop)

Resumed the parked row per the 1227 recipe (attack cluster item 1 from the
v3 for-form). Ten judged variants (repo-external scratch source, judged
through tools/judge_unit.py with the row temporarily flipped to c and
reverted after - tree clean, row stays asm):

* THE BODY IS SOLVED. `r[i].f0 / r[i].f8 / r[i].f10 += (long)mdata` in THAT
  statement order (+0x00, +0x08, +0x10) compiles register-for-register
  identical to retail's 12-insn loop body: i in a2 (addiu at body head),
  records in a1 with disps 0/0x10/8, base in a0 (addu v0,a0,v0 x3), v0/v1
  temps, slt a2-vs-a3 tail, backedge addiu a1,0x1c in the bnez delay slot.
* CLUSTER ITEM 1 (the p+8 CSE) IS DEAD: the split second IV comes from the
  r++ WALKING pointer form (two givs r and r+8, combined as $5=$6+8), not
  from long*-indexing vs struct fields - struct fields split identically.
  The INDEXED r[i] form (pointer fixed, index walks) reduces to ONE address
  giv with constant disps. This is what defeated all 7 census shapes + both
  probes: they all walked the record pointer.
* CLUSTER ITEM 4 (walk2 temperizes) DISSOLVES with the indexed body: r's
  init no longer shares the increment result (the giv init takes the copy
  role) and walk2 lands in place as addu $4,$4,4. Items 2-3 (i++ first,
  load hoisting) reproduce with the same body; item 3's load order is the
  STATEMENT order [+0x00, +0x08, +0x10] (any other order swaps the 2nd/3rd
  loads).
* THE HEAD IS THE LAST CORNER, and it is one insn-shaped delta. Retail:
  [walk1 addiu a0,4][i=0 addu a2][lw count][nop][blez + walk2-in-delay]
  [giv copy]. Every shape tested collapses to [walk1][lw][walk2][blez +
  i=0-in-delay][giv copy] (SIZE 116 = retail 120 - 4: walk2 fills the
  lw->blez hazard slot so the nop never appears, and i=0 sinks into the
  blez delay slot). Shapes tried: comma-init for (canonicalizes to the
  separate-load form), separate count load, post-inc vs pre-inc r-init,
  explicit `i = 0;` statement + empty-init for (gcc sinks it below the
  load anyway), separate base local (allocator moves base to a3), base =
  mdata + 1 (sum lands in a1, not a0), cond-form count `i < *mdata`
  (NOT hoisted: per-iteration reload + in-loop nop, SIZE 124 - rejected).
  gcc 2.6.3's pipeline refuses to place the biv zero-init between the
  parameter walk and the count load.
* FLAG EVIDENCE: -fno-strength-reduce (via the new cc.sh CC1FLAGS_EXTRA
  hook) also kills the IV split but LOSES the vars=8 pad (frameless, SIZE
  116) - the pad needs the for-form biv slot that only strength-reduce's
  loop pass allocates. Retail's flags keep strength-reduce ON; the pad law
  and the one-pointer body are both satisfied ONLY by indexed-form +
  default flags.

### W16.DAT (EU-only root file, 327700 B, lba 166) - IDENTIFIED

- TIM image: magic 0x10, flag 0x2, one image block (no CLUT), VRAM position
  (0,0), 640x256, 16 bpp; data 0x50000 B + 0x14 header = 0x50014 exactly.
  True per-sector read (the slot after the boots region - JP parks SE.VH
  in the same lba slot).
- Content: the STANDARD SONY PAL ANTI-PIRACY WARNING screen - white rules
  + cyan text on black, the "unauthorised reproduction ... criminal
  offence" + "PIRACY harms Consumers ... Customer Service number given in
  the manual" paragraphs. 64 unique colors, 26,626 non-black pixels in
  rows 0..215. Render banked repo-external (disc_work/w16_render.png,
  scripts/w16_render.py - pypng, no numpy/PIL needed).
- EU-only: no W16 string in ANY other module; the file exists only on the
  EU disc (JP parks SE.VH at that lba).

### The sces boot's config-template pool (the W16 loader context)

- baselines/sces_00269.bin carries the literal `\W16.DAT;1` at file 0x970
  (VA 0x80020170), immediately followed by `VOICE=%d` at 0x97C - AFTER the
  `cdrom:\MAINMENU.EXE;1` / `file not found\n` strings and a 6-entry
  FUNCTION-pointer table (0x80021E68..0x80021F14 - boot-stage hooks, code
  not strings), and BEFORE the gameinfo.c assert strings
  ("%s(%d):Invalid mission value in set_game_info()" etc).
- slps carries the SAME pool layout with `VOICE=%d` at the SAME file
  offset 0x970 but NO W16 string: the EU pool = JP pool + a 0xC-byte
  `\W16.DAT;1` insertion, shifting everything after by 0xC (assert strings
  +0xC; the pool pointer-table targets +0x58 total = the 0xC shift plus
  ~0x4C of additional EU strings further in the pool).
- ZERO pointer words and ZERO lui/addiu immediates reference ANY pool
  string in either boot - because the pool is not consumed by la-style
  references at all.

### The consumer: the config-template initializer family (the mechanism)

- Both boots carry an initializer family in the file 0x4ff8..0x52d0 band
  (sces VA 0x80024800-ish, slps 0x800247d0-ish) whose repeated shape is:
    move $a0, $s0
    andi $v0, $a0, 0xffff
    sltiu $v0, $v0, 2        # if ((u16)mode < 2)
    bnez -> skip
    (delay) j ... / sh $s0, 0xb28+2k($a1)   # else: store the u16 VALUE
    lui $a0, 0x8002; addiu $a0, <template_k> # from the pool
    lui $a1, 0x8002; addiu $a1, <working base>
    jal <region copy worker>  (sces 0x8002DA04, slps 0x8002DC10)
    ori $a2, <len_k>
  i.e. per-mode conditional copies of config TEMPLATES from the pool into
  a fixed working struct head (sces dst 0x8002008C, slps 0x80020080 - the
  two bases differ by exactly the 0xC W16 insertion), with an else-path
  that stores the numeric mode value into a SERIES of u16 slots at
  0x80020080+0xb28/0xb2a/0xb2c/0xb2e/0xb30/0xb32 (a ~0xB30-byte config
  struct).
- The templates include the shared high-entropy block at file 0x8C0..0x8EF
  (partly byte-identical between slps and sces - shared binary config,
  not code) plus the strings; lens seen 0xcf/0xd6/0xe2/0xea.

### The VOICE paradox resolution (leading hypothesis, testable in decode)

`VOICE=%d` and `\W16.DAT;1` are CONFIG-TEMPLATE FIELDS, not free-standing
FLOAD literals. The mode-gate resolves the cron-20261017-1227 paradox:
retail runs with mode >= 2, the else-path stores NUMBERS into the config
slots, and the literal-string default (mode < 2) branches - the only paths
that would open a file literally named "VOICE=%d" or "\W16.DAT;1" - never
execute. The 1227 window's "raw template feed" observation at the FLOAD
wrapper family was a pointer INTO the working struct under the default
branch. W16.DAT's warning display is likewise expected on the gated
branch (EU shows it when the region/anti-modchip check selects the warning
mode); retail boot takes the numeric path and execs MAINMENU.EXE.
Testable: decode the mode source ($s0 provenance at the initializer's
caller) and the working-struct consumer that builds FOpen args.

### The boots de-frame from their own baselines (new tool, disc not needed)

- scripts/boot_deframe.py (repo-external) parses the woven grid out of baselines/{sces_
  00269,slps_00270}.bin directly. MEASURED layout (both boots identical): payload [0,0x118)
  = the PRECEDING disc sector's EDC/ECC (280 B - the extraction's seek lands one sector
  early at +2072, so sector 0's own user data is NOT in the file); syncs at payload
  0x118 + k*0x930 (123 of them, verified (p-0x918) mod 0x930 == 0 x123); user chunk k =
  [0x130 + k*0x930, 0x930 + k*0x930) = 2048 B = TRUE payload [k*0x800, (k+1)*0x800); EDC/ECC
  = [0x930 + k*0x930, +280); chunk 122 truncated to 1520 B by the size stop.
- Runtime image = concat(chunks 0..122) at 0x80020000 = 0x3D5F0 B; missing tail 0x9210
  EXACTLY as banked. PROOF: the CRT0 decodes verbatim at the banked pc0s - slps 0x8002DB14
  = zero-clear 0x800663FC..0x8012C3F4, sces 0x8002D908 = clear 0x80066098..0x8012C16C.
  The carve<->runtime map: drift = carve - runtime = 0x130*(k+1) for chunk k - the
  documented drift law re-derived from first principles, now with the boots' own numbers
  (0x130*123 = 0x9210 at the window depth).
- EVERY authored absolute address in the boots (jal/j targets, lui/addiu immediates,
  branch targets) is a RUNTIME address. Any carve-space decode of boot code above chunk 0
  reads real instruction bytes from the WRONG runtime offset and mis-aimed every reference.

### CORRECTION: the 1834 "config-template initializer family" is the gameinfo.c assert/warning family

The 1834 entry read carve bytes at runtime-authored addresses (templates, worker, controller,
struct) - the mechanism it banked inverts and re-identifies as follows (all runtime-space,
scripts/boot_runtime_decode.py + boot_phase5/6/7.py):

- The "template copy workers" (sces 0x8002DA04, slps 0x8002DC10) are A0-BIOS-call thunks:
  `addiu $t2,0xa0; jr $t2; addiu $t1,0x3F` = the $t1/$t2 convention. 0x3F = printf per
  psyq's own stubs (re-provisioned /home/z/psyq-sigs/330 LIB*.LIB.json; the sig table
  confirms strcmp=A0:0x17, strlen=0x1B, strcpy=0x19, memcpy=0x2A, memset=0x2B, InitHeap=
  0x39, printf=0x3F; sprintf's workhorse with a 0x280 stack buffer sits at sces 0x8002DA54).
- The "working struct 0x8002008C" = the string "gameinfo.c" (the __FILE__ argument). The
  "template pool" = printf FORMAT STRINGS. The family is 12+ assert/warning members:
  printf("%s(%d):Invalid <FIELD> value in set_game_info()", "gameinfo.c", line) for
  mission(200), TV_MODE(207), PAUSE_DISP(214), MUTEKI_MODE(226), MAP_COUNTER_DISP(234),
  TUNE_LEVE[L](250), LEVEL(264), "Too long PARTNER NAME"(276), PLAY_RECORDING(284),
  CLEAR_LEVEL(300), PARTNER_G_NUM(316), SUPER_BLASTER(340), plus the >17 default
  "Invalid mode switch"(320). The boots literally carry gameinfo.c.
- POLARITY INVERTED vs 1834: each member tests `sltiu v0,(u16)value,2; bnez -> store` -
  value in {0,1} = VALID = stored into the config slots; value >= 2 = INVALID = the printf
  warning. The 1834 "retail runs mode >= 2 so the literal branches never execute" is
  exactly backwards - and harmless either way, because the member's own a0/a1/a2 fully
  replace the caller's args (the invalid value is never printed; the %d gets the line
  number). printf goes to the TTY/serial - invisible on retail TVs, the shipped behavior.
- Structure: setter dispatcher 0x80023DC0 (frame 0x20, s0 = the value arg) - reads a
  halfword at FIXED 0x80010000, picks base s1 = 0x800100B8 or 0x800105F0, switch(a0) over
  an 18-entry jump table at 0x80020320; cases 3/6/7 store unconditionally (sh s0,0xb2a/
  0xb30/0xb32($a1) with a1 still = 0x80010000), the others validate. Paired getter
  dispatcher 0x80024174 (table 0x80020398) returns the fields (lh (a1), lhu 2(a1),
  lhu 0xb28(a1)...). The config area lives at 0x80010000 + {0,2,0xb28..0xb36,...} - BELOW
  the boot's own load address, i.e. written where the next stage will find it.
- The setter's only 3 static callers (0x80025BE8/0x80025C34/0x80025C44, one function) are
  the PAL-mode config reset: gate = video-mode call 0x80025570 == 2 + (u16)val < 4 +
  a bit-test in D_8006671C, then setter(5,-1) / setter(3,-1) / setter(4, 0x80066014) -
  "reset MAP_COUNTER_DISP / slot 0xb2a / MUTEKI_MODE" when the console is PAL.
- VOICE PARADOX CLOSED: `VOICE=%d` is consumed ONCE, at 0x8002368C (sces; slps 0x80023664):
  sprintf(D_8006ADDC, "VOICE=%d", (s16)D_800662BC) then an on-screen text call (a0=saved
  arg, 1, -0xE0, -0x50 - overlay coordinates). It is a DEBUG STATUS OVERLAY format string
  for a voice/audio parameter - never a filename, never a config field. The 1227 window's
  FLOAD-template observation and the 1834 mode-gate hypothesis are both superseded.
- `\W16.DAT;1` (sces pool 0x80020040): ZERO references in the extracted runtime image
  (no lui/addiu pair within 8 insns, no pointer words). Its consumer lives in the missing
  tail (payload >= 0x3D5F0, disc-only) or is dead. Disc-gated, not decodable from
  baselines. The EU-only W16.DAT warning screen remains identified (1834 entry); only its
  loader address is unknown.
- Queue item 3 of 1834 REFUTED: the "shared high-entropy block at file 0x8C0..0x8EF" =
  payload 0xC0..0xEF sits INSIDE the leading 280-B EDC/ECC zone [0,0x118) - it is the

- The 1834 "6-entry FUNCTION-pointer table" at 0x80021E68..0x80021F14 = inline A0-call

### The de-frame law re-derived empirically, and the per-sector view validates it exactly

- The contiguous baseline lands ONE SECTOR EARLY: chunk k = bl[(k+1)*0x930 : +0x800]
  is file sector k+1 (file[(k+1)*0x800 : +0x800]); the 2048-B PS-X EXE header (file
  sector 0) is never present in the baseline. Syncs verified at 0x918 + k*0x930 (123).
- 122 full chunks + a 0x5F0 partial: the de-framed overlap == the per-sector file
  BYTE-FOR-BYTE for both boots (zero mismatches over file 0x800..0x3DDF0). Captured
  payload = 0x3D5F0 and missing tail = 0x9210 exactly as banked (1949); the woven
  framing never corrupts user data on the boots - it only truncates the view.
- The tail payload [0x3D5F0, 0x46800) = VA 0x8005D5F0..0x80066800 exists ONLY in the
  per-sector view. Identified residents: the CD command-name pointer table
  (0x800651D4..0x80065270, words -> 'CdlSync'..'DiskError' psyq strings), the bios.c
  $Id string (0x800654D4, v1.71 1995/12/01 makoto), the .sdata window (below), then an
  all-zero strip to payload end (loaded-but-zeroed BSS extension).

### The .sdata windows decode: they are the boots' _gp anchor area

- sces window payload 0x45FC4..0x46098 (53 words): word 0 = 0x80020040 = pointer to
  '\W16.DAT;1' - THE EU-ONLY VARIABLE. The remaining 52 words are REGION-SHARED
  (sces[4:] == slps[:] byte-exact in the true view): default pilot/high-score names as
  packed ASCII ('NONE', 'FRANK', 'REIKO', 'JOHNSON', 'SHARK', 'GHOST'), controller-tag
  fragments ' (1)'..' (D)', the CD device prefix 'bu00:', and constants 0x6981/0x6A81/
  0x2A. slps window payload 0x4632C..0x463FC (52 words) = the same table with NO W16
  word - the +4 shift the contiguous view showed is exactly the missing variable.
- CRT0 sets $gp to the window start: sces 0x8002D988 (lui $gp,0x8006; addiu
  $gp,0x5FC4 -> $gp = 0x80065FC4), slps 0x8002DB94 ($gp = 0x8006632C). The zero-clear
  ranges start at the window END (sces clears 0x80066098..0x8012C16C, slps
  0x800663FC..0x8012C3F4 - both banked numbers re-confirmed against the true view).
- The pool strings are NOT lui/addiu-referenced because the pool (0x80020000-0x80021FFF
  area) is OUTSIDE every gp window's +/-0x8000 reach; the tail data is INSIDE it. That
  is the encoding law behind the 1834/1949 "zero la-style references" observation.

### THE W16 LOADER CLOSES: sces-only function 0x8002228C, called unconditionally by the boot main

- sces boot main 0x8002180C (called from CRT0 0x8002D9A8) call sequence: stub 0x8002D900,
  config-slot clear, inits 0x8002F3C8(2)/0x8002E674(1), sub-init 0x800219BC, then at
  0x8002183C an UNCONDITIONAL jal 0x8002228C, then 0x80023AD8/0x800252C8/0x8002BF38...
- 0x8002228C (frame 0x40): ResetGraph-shaped 0x8002F508(0); video setup with 640x240
  geometry (0x80032B74(0x280,0xF0,0,0); 0x800370E4(0,0,0,0xF0)); clear + sync
  (0x8003331C); then lw $a0,($gp) = the '\W16.DAT;1' pointer (the ONLY gp+0 load in
  either boot), jal 0x8002D5B8 (file open; calls the 0x8002D620 worker, -1-checked).
  If the open returns 0 -> skip silently (epilogue). Else jal 0x8002CBA0 (a0 = handle,
  a1 = stack buffer) - THE BANKED 0x8002CBA0 CONSUMER SHAPE IDENTIFIED: it validates
  u32 == 0x10 (the TIM magic) at the buffer head, parses the TIM header fields
  (lhu 0x1C/0x1E/0x20), and loads the image - it is the boot's TIM loader/renderer.
  Then 0x8002F508(1), 0x80037590, and a bounded VSync wait: s0 = 0x96 (150 frames),
  0x8002F194(0) per frame - the warning shows for 150 VSyncs (~2.5 s at 60 Hz, 3 s at
  PAL 50 Hz), then boot proceeds.
- slps: boot main 0x80021800 (CRT0 0x8002DBB4) NEVER calls it - the call sequence has
  no such slot (0x8002F8BC(2), 0x80021964, then straight to 0x80023AB0/0x800252A0/
  0x8002C110/0x800219F0), and no gp+0 load exists anywhere in the image. The W16
  display path is EU-only end to end: string (pool) + pointer variable (.sdata word 0)
  + loader function + call site, all present only in sces.
- RESOLUTION of the queue item: the EU boot shows the Sony PAL anti-piracy warning on
  EVERY boot - there is no region/modchip gate at the call site; the only condition is
  the file open succeeding (a copied disc lacking \W16.DAT;1 boots straight through).
  It is a marking, not a check. And the reason 1949 found ZERO references in the
  runtime image: the reference is SPLIT ACROSS VIEWS - the consuming code
  (0x800222DC lw $a0,($gp)) lives in the base, the pointer variable lives in the
  missing tail (.sdata word 0), and the string is reached only through $gp. Neither
  view alone contains the whole chain.

### The psyq-negative proof: the FLoad family is NOT psyq

- Every string that names the family - "fload3", "FLOAD:fault!\n", "Cannot find
  file(%s) in fload3()\n", "No enough memory in fload3()\n", "Enough memory\n",
  "Fault CdSync in fload3()\n" - was binary-grepped against ALL 16 psyq 3.3 archives
  (LIBAPI LIBC LIBC2 LIBCARD LIBCD LIBCOMB LIBETC LIBGPU LIBGS LIBGTE LIBMATH LIBPRESS
  LIBSN LIBSND LIBSPU LIBTAP): zero hits. All 35 shipped headers grepped for "fload":
  zero hits. The queue's FileRead/EdOpen guesses do not exist in psyq 3.3 at all.
- The ONLY family-adjacent hit in the entire library set: LIBSND's symbol table
  carries SsVabTransBody and SsVabTransBodyPartly - the snd lane's verbatim-psyq
  member (banked 3530/3562), re-verified at the archive level this window.
- Conclusion: the boot FLoad family (retry wrappers, load preps, read halves) and
  fload3 are the PROJECT'S OWN source - consistent with the 2026-10-16 census (the
  boot's file-I/O cluster is the same linked source as all six game modules) and the
  8-target "\SE.VH;1"/"\SE.VB;1"/"FLOAD:fault!" string trio. The naming therefore
  closes "against the project's own FLoad lane", and the lane's provisional names
  become the member IDs below.

### The psyq-positive half: what the family CALLS takes its libcd name

- 0x80038D34 (fload3 step 6, the "CD command issuer": (0x15, &rec, 0), retried while
  it returns 0) = CdControl(u_char com, u_char *param, u_char *result) - shape-exact
  against LIBCD.H 3.3; the retry-while-0 loop is the busy-queue semantics of the
  async command issuer.
- The command constant: 0x15 = CdlSeekL (psyq 3.3 define table). fload3 seeks to the
  parsed ISO file record before reading - the record it filled at step 1 IS the seek
  parameter (banked verbatim at step 6). The flow is the canonical libcd idiom:
  parse record -> CdControl(CdlSeekL, &rec, 0) -> CdSync -> read.
- 0x8003AAFC (the read-request kicker) parks buf/count/mode globals, then issues
  (9, 0, 0, 0) gated on (status & 0xE0): 9 = CdlPause. psyq 3.3 ships NO 4-arg
  command issuer (the full Cd* declaration list checked), so the kicker is
  game-internal and the extra args are call-site padding; the pause clears prior
  streaming state before re-arming.
- 0x80038CAC = CdSync(mode, result) over impl 0x800398F8 (banked "CDSYNC NAMED"; now
  header-backed): the required result 2 = CdlComplete, and the parked read mode
  0x80 = CdlModeSpeed (double speed).
- CORRECTION / CREDIT (landed in the follow-up commit, same window): the Cdl
  CONSTANTS above were already named by the game-side census window (a182fba3,
  2026-10-16): command 0x15 = CdlSeekL ("&rec" IS the CdlLOC), 0x09 = CdlPause,
  result 2 = CdlComplete, mode 0x80 = CdlModeSpeed, against the same LIBCD.H 3.3.
  The 2104 window re-queued the 2026-10-16 late entry's item 4 without noticing
  a182fba3 had closed it 48 minutes after that entry was written. This window's

  (0x80038D34 = CdControl, shape-exact, retry-while-0 = busy-queue semantics) and
  the full-Cd*-list check that psyq 3.3 ships no 4-arg command issuer (the (9,0,0,0)
  kicker is game-internal).

### Method warning (a live drift demonstration)

  VA = vram + (off - start) math and placed the stub table at 0x8002FD10 - 0x2140

  the contiguous raw-read (0x930-byte sectors), ~0x130 of framing per 0x800 of
  user data, and 26 sectors of drift at that depth ≈ 0x1EE0 + the header offset.
  ALL boot code addressing must use the TRUE per-sector view (or the weave
  mapping (F>>11)*0x930+(F&0x7FF) when reading the baseline); the banked true VAs
  only reconcile on the true view. The committed baselines stay the verify
  oracle - this warning is about ADDRESSING, not about bytes.

  ch, void (*f)()) - the only declared psyq 3.3 API with that shape; the
  body manages ALL channels (0..10), so the name is the 3.3-era declared
  spelling of the indexed interrupt-callback setter (the concept psyq later
  spells InterruptCallback). Returns the previous handler.
- [0x10] 0x8002F080 = StopCallback (flag-gated: must be initialized): saves
  I_MASK -> pool+0x32 and DICR -> pool+0x34, masks everything (I_MASK = 0),

  returns 0.

  re-hooks HookEntryInt(B0#0x19) on the node 0x8004D2D4, restores the saved
  I_MASK and DICR, sets the flag, runs the a0=2 raw-syscall tail. ZERO
  payload callers - linked but unreached in the boot, the symmetric
  complement of [0x10].

  stores sit in the DELAY SLOTS of the FOLLOWING calls, so they store the

   FRAMING/HEADER in slps (in sces the same-numbered carve position held the

   0x4AE0 = pin interior, seed refused; 0x80024424 -> file 0x4C24 = a 0xC

materialization stub `move $v0,$s0`, falling into 0x800242D0, the real

single join corresponds to the epilogue; the getter's extra join is the
stub. Split condition = the case's return shape. Two shapes:
- s0-form: `lh $s0,X($v1)` + `j 0x800242D0` + delay `move $v0,$s0` - the
  sign-extending lh loads: case 0 (lh ($a1) - reads the selector halfword

- v0-form: `lhu $v0,X($base)` + `j 0x8002423C` + delay `sll $v0,0x10` -
  case 1 (TV_MODE 2($a1)), 3 (2($v1)), and the C-block cases 8/9/10/11/13/
  14/15/17 (0xB28..0xB36 ($a1)). They funnel into a SHARED SIGN-EXTEND
  TRAMPOLINE at 0x8002423C (`j 0x800242CC; sra $s0,$v0,0x10`) which lives
  INSIDE case 3's island as compiler fall-through sharing: case 3 is the
  only record-side lhu case, and its tail doubles as the lhu cases' exit.

setter case map mirrors 1:1 onto load offsets). Case 4 (PARTNER NAME)

CASE 12 (SUPER_BLASTER, 0x8002427C, its own island) is a DUAL-RECORD
CONSENSUS read: v0 = sra16(lhu 0x5EE($a1)) = recA+0x536; if != -1 ->
s0 = 0 -> join A. Else v0 = sra16(lhu 0xB26($a1)) = recB+0x536; s0 =
negu(sltiu(nor(v0),1)) = (recB+0x536 == -1). So get_game_info(12) returns 1
iff BOTH mission records' SUPER_BLASTER are -1, else 0 (setter domain
{-1,0}): the super blaster is armed only by mission-record consensus.

   at record A.

   builder fills BOTH record A and record B with identical defaults,
   correcting the 1334 "record B left to the runtime API" reading: per
   record, sh 2 -> +0x00 (LEVEL), sh -1 -> +0x02, the 5-byte default

   andi+sltiu from (unsigned short)val - case 0/1/8/10/11/15 <2, case 6
   <5, case 16 <4 - and the SUBTRACT form for the ranges: [1,4] as
   (u16)(val-1) < 4 (addiu -1/andi/sltiu), [-1,3] as (u16)(val+1) < 5,

THE PRINCIPLE (the window's payoff): retail runtime encodings are
layout-invariant. The true file's instruction words equal the woven
file's - the flip re-places rows in the FILE, it does not change what
the retail code encodes - so every address retail code encodes IS a
woven-era address, and the flip must NOT re-point any symbol retail
code references. Reference resolution binds to the RETAIL ENCODINGS
(the same oracle discipline as everything else); row/file positions
bind only the byte layout. The curated-table migration re-pointed
retail-encoded symbols (4/4 checked names wrong) - wrong class rule.
The re-scan must re-derive curated entries from the retail encodings,
not from row-position arithmetic. (sces's four names are the pilot
set; the same audit applies to every C-referenced curated name in all
8 targets.)
